purpose: Triheptanoin is used to treat a rare inherited condition called long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders (LC-FAOD). In these conditions, the body cannot properly break down certain fats for energy. This medicine helps provide the body with the fuel it needs to function properly.
how_it_works: Normally, your body breaks down fats to make energy, but with LC-FAOD, this process doesn't work well. Triheptanoin is a special type of fat (oil) that your body can more easily break down into a different kind of fuel called odd-chain fatty acids and ketones. These alternative fuels help your heart, muscles, and other organs get the energy they need.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach-related and include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, and an upset stomach. Some people may also experience gas or bloating. These effects are often mild and may improve over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have any liver or digestive problems before starting this medicine. Because it is an oil taken by mouth, it should be taken with food to help reduce stomach upset. Always follow your doctor's dosing instructions carefully, as the right dose depends on your body weight.
typical_dosing: Triheptanoin is taken by mouth as a liquid oil, usually mixed into food or a drink. The dose is based on your body weight and is typically split into four equal doses throughout the day with meals or snacks. Your doctor will calculate the exact amount that is right for you.
